hints.content:
$\displaystyle \lim_{x\to -4}g(x)$ represents the limit of $g$ as $x$ approaches $-4$.

Although the function isn't defined at $x=-4$, the $y$-values seem to approach a distinct value as the $x$-values approach $-4$.

![The graph of function g has arrows pointing along the curve, up to the right and down to the left, to the open circle.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/58c12e84bc2c3e292ecd669201d57e91f9c3f945)

The limit seems to be somewhere between $y=-6$ and $y=-5$, but slightly closer to $y=-5$.

![The graph of function g has a dashed horizontal line intersecting the open circle between y = negative 5 and y = negative 6, closer to y = negative 5.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/48012f19743998651208aa6f81e97a07d4355c9e)

question.content:
The function $g$ is defined for all real numbers except for $x=-4$.

![Function g is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 8. The graph consists of a curve. The curve starts in quadrant 3 and moves upward through an open circle at x = negative 4, just below y = negative 5. The curve continues upward and ends in quadrant 1.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/a9afb3e28cbdea42ff16e6bb4169bcdd2e7dced2)

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -4}g(x)$ ?**
